what: The card runs as one stock Mastra workflow whose three steps each start the stage program as its own process
why: Each stage already has its own harness and store, and Mastra's observability database takes a process-wide lock; running the stages in one process would make the review and the builder fight for the writer
evidence: machine/parent/workflow.mjs starts build, remediation and landing through machine/parent/stages.mjs; machine/run.test.mjs runs the real entry point with stub programs and reads three succeeded stages in order

what: The run record is one JSON file per run under /var/lib/julia-dashboard/state/machine-runs/
why: A run is read as a whole, so one file needs no join and no schema migration, and the dashboard already reads that state folder
evidence: MACHINE_RUNS_DIR is honoured by both sides; a served dashboard listed a seeded record and its detail page
result: machine/parent/store.mjs writes atomically with a temporary file and a rename

what: Stalled is derived when the record is read, never stored
why: Storing it would need a second writer to notice a dead process, and a dead process cannot write; the reader has the clock
evidence: shownStatus returns running until heartbeatAt is older than the record's own idleLimitMs; a served run with a two-hour-old heartbeat showed a stalled pill
result: machine/parent/store.mjs, dashboard/lib/machine-runs.js, tested on both sides

what: The idle limit travels inside the record instead of being a constant in each reader
why: Two copies of ten minutes would drift, and the page would then disagree with the machine about the same run
evidence: record.idleLimitMs is written at run start from MACHINE_IDLE_LIMIT_MIN; dashboard/lib/machine-runs.js reads it from the record
result: machine/parent/store.test.mjs covers the fallback and the env override

what: The run writes a heartbeat every thirty seconds, and the stages are spawned asynchronously
why: spawnSync would block the event loop and stop the heartbeat, so a thirty-minute build would read as stalled
evidence: runStage resolves on the child's close event; machine/run.mjs keeps a 30s interval that rewrites heartbeatAt
result: the run test that fails at remediation still shows the record's later stages pending

what: The pull request names JUL-329, the card this session bills to
why: The scorecard prices a card from the sessions its own kickoff named, and this session was started for JUL-329; a slice's own PR can name the slice only when a session was kicked off naming that slice
evidence: docs/scorecards/JUL-330.md would print Cost: unknown; docs/scorecards/JUL-329.md prints a measured cost, and node scripts/check-branch-pr.mjs passed repository-hygiene on PR #433
result: recorded in the PR body's Deviation section

what: The runs pages are force-dynamic and carry no meta refresh
why: A meta refresh in the body is not valid in the app router, and a dynamic page recomputes on every request, which is what "a new run appears within one minute" needs
evidence: curl against the served dashboard returned the new run without a restart after the record file changed

what: scripts/start-machine.mjs is deleted in the same change that replaces it
why: A second entry point would keep its own state file and drift from the run records
evidence: grep over the repository finds no live reference; the old test file was removed with it
result: machine/run.mjs and machine/parent/README.md carry the entry point

what: Each stage gets its own JULIA_TRACES_DIR folder, and the parent deletes MASTRA_OBSERVABILITY_DB_PATH and MASTRA_DB_PATH from the child's environment
why: Mastra's observability database is single-writer and takes a lock; a child pointed at the parent's open file records nothing at all, which is how a run can leave an empty trace while spending money
evidence: node --test machine/parent/usage.test.mjs; the stages test reads the child env and finds JULIA_TRACES_DIR set and both inherited paths gone
result: usage.mjs stageEnvironment; the stage's tokens, cost and elapsed time are read from the files it left, after it exits

what: A stage that succeeded but left no model rows is flagged on the record and on the page; a stage that failed is not
why: A failure before the first model call legitimately leaves nothing, and a warning there would be noise that hides the real empty-trace fault
evidence: store.test.mjs 'a stage that ran and recorded no model rows says so, a stage that failed does not'
result: step.warning, read back by dashboard usageCells and rendered in the run detail page

what: Cost is shown as dollars when the trace prices the calls, as 'free model' only when every model the stage used is named :free, and otherwise as 'cost unknown'
why: Claiming a free model for an unpriced paid model would tell Todd a spend that never happened
evidence: machine/parent/usage.test.mjs and dashboard/lib/machine-runs.test.mjs cover paid, free, unpriced and mixed
result: describeUsage in usage.mjs and usageCells in the dashboard

what: The stall watcher marks the run before it pings, and the record carries pingedAt so a second pass sends nothing
why: A ping that is sent before the mark is lost and repeats on the next tick; the mark makes the pass idempotent
evidence: machine/watch.test.mjs 'a run quiet past its idle limit is marked stalled and Todd is told once'; formal/machine PingOnce also holds this
result: machine/watch.mjs watchOnce; store.stall returns null when pingedAt is already set

what: The watcher runs from a systemd timer every minute beside the dashboard's own timers, through the julia-agents wrapper
why: A dead process cannot send its own ping, so the ping needs a pass outside the run; the wrapper keeps the Linear key in the vault rather than on disk
evidence: dashboard/ops/julia-machine-watch.service and .timer are in the installer's UNITS and TIMERS; install-service.test.mjs iterates both lists
result: one pass a minute after a 60s boot delay

what: The stock session.thread.switch replaces the direct write to mastra_threads.updatedAt
why: The switch both selects the thread and makes it newest on its own, so the direct edit was a second writer of state the SDK already owns
evidence: /tmp probe showed the switch bumping updatedAt; machine/remediation/thread-switch.test.mjs boots, creates a second thread, switches back and asserts the id
result: makeNewest is deleted; bootOnThread asserts the session is on the target thread or throws

what: Subagent calls carry tracingContext.currentSpan taken from the workflow step
why: The stock subagent tool forwards context.tracingContext to the agent it starts; without it the agent run begins a new root trace
evidence: spikes/stock-workflow-proof/trace-tree.mjs produced one trace with workflow_run, workflow_step 'review', agent_run 'subagent-execute' and model_generation nested in that order; the earlier spike without it produced a separate root
result: harness.mjs agentContext, used by the shipping review step and the merge retro step

what: A fresh subagent's model rows carry no thread id, and the run record does not pretend otherwise
why: The stock controller sets threadId null and strips the thread and resource keys for a non-forked subagent; only a forked subagent gets a cloned thread, and the machine's agents are not the builder's conversation
evidence: agent-controller-UmAUfVvn.js sets controller.threadId null and deletes MASTRA_THREAD_ID_KEY on the non-forked path; the trace-tree spike's metric_events rows held threadId null
result: the run's join key is the stage's trace file and its span ids, recorded on the step's usage; the trace tree itself is one per stage
